status: M0 plan for the new OfficeIMO front-door package (no project exists yet; NuGet ID registered with two unlisted 0.1.x versions from 2022).

notes: Word.Html and Markdown.Html bring OfficeIMO.Html + AngleSharp; include them so the front door keeps HTML import and Markdown raw-HTML fidelity (Word.Markdown no longer references Word.Html).
Reader.All brings 31 reader handlers; confirm that is wanted (the design lists "Reader" without scope).
Workflows is not referenced: it brings Invoicing, Project, OCR, Visio, DjVu, CHM, EPUB, Email and is net8/net10 only.

publicTypes: OfficeConverter (static): Convert(string source, string destination, OfficeConversionOptions options = null) : OfficeConversionReport; Convert(Stream source, OfficeFormat sourceFormat, Stream destination, OfficeFormat target, OfficeConversionOptions options = null); ConvertAsync(...) twins; ConvertAsync(IEnumerable<string> sources, string outputDirectory, OfficeFormat target, OfficeBatchOptions options = null) : Task<OfficeBatchReport>; Analyze(string source, string destination, OfficeConversionOptions options = null) : OfficeConversionReport (proposed); Register(IOfficeConversionRoute route) (proposed, for Tier 2 routes)

OfficeFormat (enum): Docx, Doc, Dotx, Docm, Xlsx, Xls, Xlsb, Xlsm, Pptx, Ppt, Pdf, Md, Html, Png, Jpeg, Svg, Tiff, Webp, ... (one value per file format; Core already has OfficeDocumentFormat - see openQuestions)

OfficeConversionOptions: target-specific option bags (Word = WordPdfExportOptions, ...), FailOnLoss, conflict policy, limits; replaces OfficeWorkflowConversionOptions and Word/Excel/PowerPoint *DocumentConversionOptions

OfficeBatchOptions: MaxParallelism, ResumeFrom, OutputDirectory, Recursive, Extensions, ConflictPolicy, limits, Load/Save (JSON job file); replaces OfficeConversionJob, OfficeConversionBatchRequest and builder state
OfficeBatchReport / OfficeBatchItemReport: per-item OfficeConversionReport, totals, elapsed, resume state; replaces OfficeConversionBatchResult/Report and OfficeConversionJobRunReport
OfficeDocument (static): Inspect(string path, OfficeInspectOptions options = null) for any format (design: Lifecycle)
absorbs: OfficeIMO.Workflows Batches/ and ConversionJobs/ (checkpointing, resume, publication guard) - port to netstandard2.0
*ToPdfBytes helpers in Word, PowerPoint, Excel.Pdf (and Tier 2 *.Pdf adapters: 400 files call ToPdfBytes, mostly tests)

conflicts: OfficeIMO.Core already declares 101 public types in the OfficeIMO namespace (OfficeConversionResult<,>, OfficeOutputResult<>, OfficeDocumentFormat, OfficeDocumentModel, OfficePageOrientation, OfficeConversionLossPolicy, IOfficeConversionReport, ...). The rule "the OfficeIMO namespace holds only OfficeConverter, OfficeFormat and the batch types" conflicts with Core unless Core moves to OfficeIMO.Core (a repo-wide break) or the rule is relaxed to "OfficeIMO namespace = Core shared types + the converter".
OfficeColor and the drawing types live in OfficeIMO.Drawing (374 Core types), not OfficeIMO.
OfficeDocumentFormat (Core) and the planned OfficeFormat overlap; keep one.
openQuestions: OfficeIMO.Core already places 101 public types in the OfficeIMO namespace; see OfficeIMO.json conflicts.

Dropping the Windows-only net472 TFM means .NET Framework consumers run the netstandard2.0 build. #if NETFRAMEWORK workarounds (Word Save snapshot, Excel non-seekable stream save, PDF NET472 branches) must become runtime checks, and the netstandard2.0 build must be tested on .NET Framework 4.7.2 (PSWriteOffice on Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the main consumer).

Static From{Source} on a type owned by another package (WordDocument.FromHtml in OfficeIMO.Word.Html, WordDocument.FromMarkdown, MarkdownDocument.FromHtml, WordDocument.FromPdf) is only possible with C# 14 static extension members. The SDK supports them for netstandard2.0 targets, but callers on older language versions (.NET Framework projects default to C# 7.3, Windows PowerShell) must call the containing static class directly. Alternative: keep instance forms on the source (pdf.ToWord(), html.ToWordDocument()) as the only adapter shape.

C# forbids out parameters on async methods, so "To{Target}/From{Source} have an overload with out OfficeConversionReport" cannot cover the async forms (FromHtmlAsync, LoadResultAsync, ToWordDocumentResultAsync). Choose: async forms return a (TDocument, OfficeConversionReport) result type, or async forms only throw/ignore loss.

Package IDs OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf and OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf flip direction (PDF->Word reconstruction today, Word->PDF export after). Same NuGet ID with an unrelated API is a silent break for anyone pinning 3.5.x; MIGRATION.md and the release notes must say so explicitly, or the export adapters take new IDs.

Word image export is built on the PDF writer+reader+renderer (WordPageImageExport). Keeping image export in OfficeIMO.Word without the PDF engine requires splitting OfficeIMO.Pdf into a composition/pagination core that paints to OfficeIMO.Drawing (Core) and a PDF writer. That is a large engine refactor; the cheaper option is to move Word image export to OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf (or a new OfficeIMO.Word.Imaging that references Pdf) and accept that Word image export needs the PDF engine. PowerPoint does not have this problem (its scene renderer already targets OfficeIMO.Drawing).
